text.p: Gold prices tumbled sharply on Thursday afternoon, extending early losses which took values well below the key $350 an ounce level.
The gold market breached interim support at $348 and looked poised to extend its recent slide to 3-1/4 year lows, dealers said.
"It looks terrible. It never even got close to $350 after breaking below it. There's no direction but down," a dealer said.
Bullion fixed at $349.25 in the afternoon, virtually unchanged from the morning's fixing of $349.30 but down from Wednesday's London close of $350.80/$351.30.
But shortly after the fixing, gold dipped lower to test the nearby support level at $348, and was potentially headed towards week's low of $346.
"If it goes below, gold's going to be in real trouble," one noted. An eventual target was $340 an ounce, a significant support level from 1993.
Earlier this week prices had rallied dramatically, hitting a high above $357, only to resume its steep fall.
Several dealers said they suspected central bank selling was behind the latest decline.
Fresh institutional selling had come into the market in early trading, mimicking a similar move on Wednesday morning, dealers said.
"The timing was the same as yesterday suggesting a selling programme. This was quality selling," a dealer said.
A spike in short term lease rates also appeared to suggest central bank selling, he added.
The Dutch central bank announced earlier this month it had sold 300 tonnes of gold from its reserves, deepening the market's bearish tone.
Besides the selling pressure, gold's fundamentals gave little reason to expect a lasting bounce, dealers said.
The dollar and stock markets were surging, removing incentive to invest in gold and fears of more central bank sales and producer hedging sent a chill through the market.
By contrast to gold, silver was barely changed from Wednesday's close, at $4.90/$4.92. Tiny dips in the price stopped at around $4.87 an ounce before bouncing back up.
Platinum, however, was closely following gold and fixed at a new 3-1/4 year low in the afternoon of $352.75 an ounce, down $2.00 from Wednesday's London close.
Palladium was little changed at $121.50/$122.50. --Lida Poletz, London newsroom +44 171 542 2936
